page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4 is an Arm-based general-purpose instance featuring the arm64 CPU architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs paired with 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio with exactly 4.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware profile does not include graphics accelerators, operating with zero GPUs, and includes no local ephemeral storage.

Storage operations rely entirely on remote network storage interfaces due to the absence of bundled local NVMe or SSD capacity. Furthermore, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Dedicated vCPU allocation ensures steady execution without resource contention from burstable thread scheduling, while the Arm instruction set emphasizes hardware efficiency and resource density for standard virtualized footprints.

Workload compatibility requires binaries and dependencies compiled for the arm64 platform. The 4-vCPU and 16.0 GB memory footprint aligns with middle-tier web servers, microservice containers, build farm nodes for Arm software, and general enterprise application hosting. It is not suitable for applications requiring local high-IOPS scratch disks, GPU-accelerated computing, or legacy x86 binary dependencies.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-4 is an arm64 general-purpose virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of memory, delivering a balanced 4.0 GB per core. The instance operates without discrete GPU accelerators and includes no local storage, requiring external block storage for data persistence. It also provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With dedicated core assignment and standard general-purpose memory density, the system offers predictable execution and power-efficient processing for modern architectures. Its design suits production web hosting, containerized microservices, development pipelines, and general cloud workloads that are compiled for 64-bit Arm environments.
